newsitem.title: EGYPT: Israeli politician says settlements blocking peace.
newsitem.headline: Israeli politician says settlements blocking peace.

text.p: The leader of the leftist Israeli Meretz party said on Sunday that the Jewish state's settlement policies were the biggest obstacle to Middle East peace.
"Settlements are the main stumbling block ahead of the peace process," Yossi Sarid told reporters after meeting Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa.
"We do not expect that the Palestinians and Israelis will sign a deal on Hebron soon because of the settlements," said Sarid, environment minister in the former Labour government.

Peace talks between Israel and the Palestinians are deadlocked over a long-delayed Israeli troop redeployment from the West Bank town of Hebron where 400 Jewish settlers live among 100,000 Palestinians.

The former Labour government had agreed on the redeployment but the rightwing government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu wants to renegotiate the deal for security concerns. The Palestinians want to implement the deal without changes.
Sarid's Meretz party has always favoured a Palestinian state and is on the record advocating the evacuation of Jewish settlements in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.
Sarid, who arrived in Cairo earlier for a four-day visit, also wants Israel to withdraw from occupied Arab lands.
But Netanyahu has raised Arab ire by refusing to hand over occupied territories. He has also lifted a ban imposed by the Labour government on building Jewish settlements on these lands.
Sarid, a member of Israel's Knesset, said that his party would try its best to put an end to Netanyahu's policies.
